newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-SAMPRAS, HINGIS TO RULE CENTRE COURT.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SAMPRAS, HINGIS TO RULE CENTRE COURT.

text.p: World number one Pete Sampras and the rising star of women's tennis, Martina Hingis, are poised to dominate centre court at the Australian Open again on Thursday.

Sampras, who beat hapless Romanian qualifier Dinu Pescariu in the opening round on Tuesday, faces a tougher Romanian, Adrian Voinea, while Swiss prodigy Hingis, first round victor over Barbara Rittner of Germany, meets experienced American Lisa Raymond.

World number one Sampras and fourth-seeded Hingis both showed good form in the opening round of the tournament, which has so far lost four women's and three men's seeds, including 1996 champion and world number six Boris Becker.

Sampras lost just eight games against Pescariu despite being unhappy with the softness of the balls, while Hingis overcame a brief loss of temper that saw her toss her racket into the net before disposing of Rittner 6-1 7-5.

Austria's "King of Clay", fifth seed Thomas Muster, who is waging his ninth Australian Open campaign, looks to have a fight on his hands on Melbourne Park's hardcourt Rebound Ace surface against South African Grant Stafford.
Stafford, ranked world 78, has beaten the 1995 French Open champion twice in their three encounters so far, though they have not met since Stafford's victory in Adelaide in 1994.

In Thursday night's feature matches, Slovakia's Karol Kucera will be on the receiving end of third seed Goran Ivanisevic's thunderous serve while crowd favourite Chanda Rubin of the United States, seeded 15, confronts France's Sandrine Testud.
Taking a rest will be men's second seed Michael Chang and women's top seed Steffi Graf, who both breezed through second round matches in straight sets on Wednesday.

Graf has vowed to carry on through the tournament even though her father, Peter Graf, risks a jail term in Germany for tax evasion if found guilty in a verdict expected hours before the women's final on January 25.
